newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan says plans bigger 97/98 investment.
newsitem.headline: Nissan says plans bigger 97/98 investment.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Thursday it would increase its parent capital investment in the next business year starting in April 1997 to around 110 billion yen, up from a planned 80 billion yen in 1996/97.
"Our capital investment for the next business year is likely to be around 110 billion yen, mainly for development and production equipment for new models," a Nissan spokesman said.
In December, Nissan president Yoshikazu Hanawa said the firm would introduce eight new models in calendar 1997. Nissan launched five new models and several partially remodelled cars last year.

But its domestic market share fell to a record low of 20.8 percent in 1996, below the previous record low of 21.2 percent in 1994, due to slow development of recreational vehicles, whose sales are booming in Japan.

A spokesman for Toyota Motor Corp, Japan's biggest carmaker, said the company has not yet decided its 1997 investment. But the spokesman said the parent company capital investment in 1997/98 will be at least as much as the planned 300 billion yen for 1996/97.
